Question Choices: If a shape is 5 square decimeters, how many square centimeters is that?
Hints: Use 10 centimetres along each side of a square decimetre, so its area is 10 times 10 square centimetres.
Solution: 1 decimetre = 10 centimetres, so 1 square decimetre = 10 x 10 = 100 square centimetres. Thus 5 square decimetres = 5 x 100 = 500 square centimetres.

Question Choices: Shape C has 30 square units. Shape D has 25 square units. Which shape covers more space? : C D
Hints: Count equal-size squares covering the surface without gaps or overlaps.
Solution: Both use the same square unit. Since 30 > 25, shape C has more area.

Question Choices: If a shape has 6 square decimeters, how many square centimeters is that?
Hints: Use 10 centimetres along each side of a square decimetre, so its area is 10 times 10 square centimetres.
Solution: 1 square decimetre = 100 square centimetres. Thus 6 square decimetres = 6 x 100 = 600 square centimetres.

Question Choices: Select. The same square can be measured as 25 square centimeters. It can also be measured as 1 square decimeter if the unit is larger. Does this mean one measurement is wrong? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: Use 10 centimetres along each side of a square decimetre, so its area is 10 times 10 square centimetres.
Solution: Yes. One square decimetre equals 100 square centimetres, not 25. Thus the two stated measurements cannot both describe the same square correctly.
